Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings  
• 48-year-old man with 3-day history of frequent watery stools (≈5–6/day) preceded by two episodes of vomiting; no blood, no abdominal pain; subjective low-grade fever day 1; poor oral intake and feels dehydrated.  
• PMH asthma; no regular medications other than PRN salbutamol.  
• FHx colorectal cancer (father), HTN (father), type 2 DM (mother).  
• Lives alone; non-smoker; minimal alcohol.

Working diagnosis  
• Acute viral gastroenteritis (high likelihood) – consistent with abrupt onset, self-limited course, initial vomiting, watery stool, absence of red-flag features.

Considerations  
• Bacterial food-borne gastroenteritis (medium likelihood) – similar time-course; will monitor for persistent fever, blood, or worsening pain.  
• Inflammatory bowel disease or other structural pathology (low likelihood currently) – consider if symptoms persist >1 week, recur, or red-flags develop.

Management  
• Oral rehydration therapy (e.g., Dioralyte) – dosing per package instructions.  
• Paracetamol PRN for fever/aches.  
• Advise rest and remain off work until diarrhoea-free for 24–48 h.  
• Red-flag advice: seek review if unable to keep fluids down, significant abdominal pain, blood in stool, fever >38 °C, or symptoms >7 days.  
• Follow-up: telehealth or face-to-face in 3-5 days if not improving.

  • Discussed balanced diet and regular physical activity once recovered (details not recorded).

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Viral gastroenteritis – High likelihood; classic abrupt onset vomiting then 3 days watery diarrhoea, self-limiting course, no red-flag features.  
2. Bacterial food-borne gastroenteritis – Medium likelihood; similar presentation though lacking clear food exposure or high fever.  
3. Inflammatory bowel disease – Low likelihood; acute, isolated episode without blood, pain, or chronic pattern.
